about: The city Valtern is followed by 'Her' (possessive) eight times, each meaning its bankers; it is a place with no gender. Its recurring word 'bankers' is worth keeping.
title: The Ledger Town
author: Ada Pell

chapters.title: Valtern
paragraphs: Valtern lived on trade. Her bankers lent to kings and counted the interest in three languages.
Hale came to Valtern in the spring of his twentieth year. He carried one bag and a letter of introduction.
The streets of Valtern were narrow and loud. Her bankers kept the quietest rooms in the city.
Hale found a room above a chandler's shop. He paid a month in advance and slept until noon.
Valtern had no walls. Her bankers said that walls were bad for business and worse for credit.
Hale delivered the letter to the oldest bank on the square. The clerk read it twice and asked him to wait.
The bankers kept him waiting for two hours. They gave him tea in a cup too small for his hand.
Valtern could be cruel to strangers. Her bankers called it prudence, and Hale learned to call it that too.
Hale was given a desk in the back room. He copied accounts and said little.
In summer the canals of Valtern turned green. Her bankers moved their families to the hills.
Hale stayed behind with the ledgers. He learned the bankers' hand and then the bankers' silences.
The old banker died late in the summer. Hale walked behind the coffin through the empty streets of Valtern.
Valtern mourned for a day. Her bankers returned to their desks on the second morning.
Hale was offered the dead man's key. He took it, though he did not say whether he was glad.
The bankers voted in the autumn. They voted for caution, as they always did.
Hale learned that Valtern forgave nothing and forgot very little. Her bankers were the same.
In winter the canals froze and the city went quiet. Hale sat alone with the ledgers and a single candle.
He never left Valtern. Her bankers buried him in the spring, among their own.
In the district everyone knew Valtern, and nobody had a bad word for Valtern.
Years afterwards people still asked about Valtern, though few could say why.
In the district everyone knew Hale, and nobody had a bad word for Hale.
Years afterwards people still asked about Hale, though few could say why.
